the development of a QSAR model to predict the effects of steroids on DNA replication in an estrogen receptor-free system.
the development of a QSAR model for a non-estrophilic steroid pharmacophore.

the observed effects of steroids on the HeLa cell-free DNA replication system were not due to interactions with estrogenic receptors, but rather were due to a pharmacophore that is independent of estrogen receptors.
a QSAR model was constructed for a set of 17 steroids, and a pharmacophore for the estrogen receptor-independent effects was defined.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the estrogen receptor is not the only target for steroids.
QSARs can be used to describe the effect of steroids on cellular replication in a receptor-independent manner.
the estrogen receptor is not necessary for steroids to modulate DNA replication, and that the pharmacophore for this activity is distinct from the classical estrogen receptor.
